_about: Reference notes for each synthetic test document. All documents are fictional. Nothing here is compared automatically; it is context for a human reviewing the extracted position.
_pii_note: Every document deliberately contains identity data. The extractor must isolate financial fields from identity fields and report identity only as types, never values.

01_bank_statement_meridian.pdf.title: Bank statement
01_bank_statement_meridian.pdf.layout: Ruled tables, two pages, multiple accounts plus a transaction ledger
tests: sub-account versus total aggregation
look-back transfer detection from a ledger memo
recurring income identified from transaction descriptions
traps: The $500.00 movement on 08 Jan is between the holder's own accounts. It is neither income nor a gift.
Total on deposit is a sum of the three accounts above it. Adding it to them double-counts $153,222.67.
The Opening Balance column must not be read as the current balance.

02_brokerage_equity_harborview.pdf.title: Brokerage and equity portfolio statement
02_brokerage_equity_harborview.pdf.layout: Dense seven-column holdings grid with a negative cash sweep and an allocation band
tests: read the portfolio total from a summary band rather than a table row
negative cash sweep recorded as an obligation, not a negative asset
cost basis column must not be mistaken for market value
quarterly income must not be read as monthly
traps: The CASH SWEEP line is negative (-$3,775.27). It is a margin debit, which is a liability.
Cost Basis sits immediately left of Market Value. Reading it yields $331,804.12 instead of $412,860.44.
Income this period of $4,286.65 is a quarterly figure, not a monthly one.

03_ssa_award_letter.pdf.title: Social Security award letter
03_ssa_award_letter.pdf.layout: Narrative prose only, zero tables, amounts embedded in sentences
tests: amounts embedded in sentences
gross versus net distinction
COLA language
traps: The deposited amount of $2,009.10 is net of the Medicare Part B premium. Gross benefit is $2,184.00.
There is no table anywhere in this document. A table-only extractor returns nothing.

04_pension_annuity_crestline.pdf.title: Pension and annuity election statement
04_pension_annuity_crestline.pdf.layout: Benefit election with a conditional survivor continuation and a COLA rider
tests: survivor benefit is conditional, not current income
annual figure must be converted and the conversion flagged
net versus gross after a health deduction
traps: The 50% survivor continuation of $821.25 is payable only on the death of the primary annuitant. It is not current income.
The annual figure of $19,710.00 and the monthly figure of $1,642.50 describe the same benefit. Counting both doubles it.
The deposited figure is net of a $118.00 retiree health deduction.

05_form_1099r.pdf.title: Form 1099-R
05_form_1099r.pdf.layout: IRS box-numbered grid, gross distribution against taxable amount
tests: box-numbered layout rather than labelled rows
gross distribution is not the same as taxable amount
an annual distribution must not be read as monthly
traps: Box 1 gross distribution of $28,400.04 is annual. The monthly equivalent is $2,366.67.
Box 2a taxable amount of $26,118.04 is lower than box 1. Neither is a monthly income figure.
Box 4 federal withholding of $2,840.00 is not an expense of the resident.

06_ltc_policy_summary.pdf.title: Long-term care policy summary
06_ltc_policy_summary.pdf.layout: Benefit schedule with a lifetime pool, elimination period and inflation rider
tests: a benefit pool is coverage, not an asset
daily benefit must be converted to a monthly equivalent correctly
the premium is an expense while the pool is not an asset
traps: The $328,500 lifetime maximum is coverage. Adding it to assets overstates the estate by a third of a million dollars.
The daily benefit of $210.00 is not $210 per month.
The 90-day elimination period means no benefit is payable for the first three months of a claim.

07_family_asset_debt_worksheet.pdf.title: Family-prepared asset and debt worksheet
07_family_asset_debt_worksheet.pdf.layout: Informal worksheet with unknown placeholders and arithmetic that does not reconcile
tests: unknown values must stay unknown rather than becoming zero
a stated total that disagrees with its line items must raise a conflict
approximate figures must be flagged as approximate
traps: Two lines carry ??? and must be recorded as unknown, never as $0.
The stated total of $240,000 does not equal the sum of the listed lines. Both figures must be surfaced.
Several figures are prefixed 'about' and are approximations.
This document was prepared by a family member and carries no institutional verification.

08_property_settlement_statement.pdf.title: Property settlement statement
08_property_settlement_statement.pdf.layout: ALTA-style closing statement with a superseded net-to-seller figure
tests: a future-dated lump sum is not a current balance
a superseded figure must be replaced and the original raised as a warning
the mortgage payoff is a liability extinguished at closing
traps: An earlier net-to-seller figure of $275,000.00 appears on page 1 and is superseded by $268,412.55.
Settlement is dated 30 April 2026, in the future. The proceeds are not a current asset.
The gross sale price of $412,000 is not the amount the seller receives.

09_consolidated_couple_vance.pdf.title: Consolidated household summary (couple)
09_consolidated_couple_vance.pdf.layout: Two residents, per-owner attribution across joint and individual accounts
tests: ownership attribution across joint and individual accounts
a joint account must not be double-counted against both residents
household totals against per-resident totals
traps: The joint checking balance appears once under Joint. Attributing it to both residents doubles it.
Only one spouse receives the pension. The other receives Social Security only.
The household total is a sum. It is not an additional account.

10_401k_statement_northstar.pdf.title: 401(k) participant statement
10_401k_statement_northstar.pdf.layout: Participant statement with vesting, employer match and an outstanding plan loan
tests: vested balance against total balance
an outstanding participant loan is a liability inside a retirement asset
year-to-date contribution columns are not balances
traps: The outstanding participant loan of $12,480.00 is a debt against the plan, not part of the balance available.
Total balance $284,610.33 and vested balance $276,118.21 differ. Only the vested amount is accessible.
YTD contributions of $7,200 is a flow, not a balance.

11_ira_rmd_notice.pdf.title: Traditional IRA statement and RMD notice
11_ira_rmd_notice.pdf.layout: IRA balance with a required minimum distribution schedule and withholding election
tests: the IRA balance is an asset while the RMD is an income stream
an annual RMD must be converted to monthly and flagged
the prior year-end balance is the RMD basis, not the current balance
traps: The account balance and the RMD are two different things. Counting the RMD as an additional asset double-counts it.
The RMD of $9,884.40 is annual. The monthly equivalent is $823.70.
The 12/31/2025 balance of $258,400.19 is the RMD basis, not today's balance of $261,772.08.

12_real_estate_appraisal.pdf.title: Residential real estate appraisal
12_real_estate_appraisal.pdf.layout: Uniform residential appraisal with a comparable sales grid and a reconciled opinion of value
tests: the opinion of value is the asset, not the comparable sale prices
the assessed value differs from the appraised value
an outstanding mortgage against the property is a separate liability
traps: The comparable sales grid lists three other properties' prices. None of them is the subject's value.
County assessed value of $338,500 is not the market value of $412,000.
The prior appraisal of $369,000 from 2021 is historic and superseded.

13_mortgage_statement.pdf.title: Mortgage account statement
13_mortgage_statement.pdf.layout: Monthly servicing statement with principal, escrow and a payoff quote
tests: principal balance is the liability, not the monthly payment
escrow balance is an asset held by the servicer, not a reduction of the debt
the payoff quote exceeds the principal balance
traps: The escrow balance of $2,418.60 is money held on the borrower's behalf. It does not reduce the principal.
The payoff amount of $128,812.78 is higher than the principal balance of $128,400.18 because of accrued interest.
The monthly payment of $1,412.60 includes escrow. Only $972.14 of it services the loan.

14_reverse_mortgage_hecm.pdf.title: Reverse mortgage (HECM) statement
14_reverse_mortgage_hecm.pdf.layout: Home equity conversion mortgage with a growing balance and an available credit line
tests: an available credit line is borrowing capacity, not an asset
the loan balance increases over time rather than amortising
accrued interest and MIP are part of the balance owed
traps: Available line of credit of $84,200.00 is money that can be borrowed. It is not cash the resident holds.
The balance grows every month. Last year's figure understates today's debt.
Net principal limit is not equity and is not an asset.

15_credit_card_medical_debt.pdf.title: Credit card statement and medical account summary
15_credit_card_medical_debt.pdf.layout: Revolving card balance with minimum payment, plus itemised patient balances
tests: minimum payment is not the balance owed
an insurance-adjusted patient responsibility is the real liability
a payment plan instalment is a monthly obligation
traps: The minimum payment due of $192.00 is not the debt. The balance is $8,412.77.
The billed charges of $18,440.00 are not owed. Patient responsibility after insurance is $3,187.42.
The available credit of $6,587.23 is borrowing capacity, not an asset.

16_life_insurance_cash_value.pdf.title: Whole life policy annual statement
16_life_insurance_cash_value.pdf.layout: Cash surrender value against death benefit, with an outstanding policy loan
tests: cash surrender value is an asset while the death benefit is not
an outstanding policy loan reduces both the surrender value and the death benefit
the net surrender value is what is actually realisable
traps: The death benefit of $150,000 is not an asset of the living insured.
The gross cash value of $48,220.14 is reduced by an $8,400 policy loan. Net surrender value is $39,820.14.
Surrender charges apply until policy year 20.

17_assisted_living_billing.pdf.title: Assisted living community invoice
17_assisted_living_billing.pdf.layout: Monthly community invoice with base rate, care level charges and ancillary items
tests: recurring monthly cost of care
a one-off community fee is not a recurring expense
a level-of-care increase changes the forward-looking monthly figure
traps: The one-time community fee of $4,500 is not a monthly expense.
The current invoice total of $7,842.00 includes one-off items. The recurring monthly cost is $6,942.00.
The care level increases to level 3 from March, raising the recurring figure to $7,342.00.
